I participated in my fair share of recruiting for the game. I find
that nearly everyone I get the time to show the game to likes it a
lot. Then there are a lot social questions. If a player likes the game
but doesn't get along very well with people in the playgroup - they'll
stop showing up. That's just hit and miss.
For example, in Ireland, I got a group of friends to all start
together, that way we had games with a group that knew each other and
once they got more into the game, they even travelled for tournaments.
To get people into the game it is very important to have at least one
person with a large collection that lends cards out, so people can
build decks and look at cards. You should have decks for their
beginnings. I do not recomend the standard learner decks - it can be
very fustrating to a player to have a deck that cannot do much, even
if no one else can do much! The game is much more fun when your deck
does a lot and well, so start them off with a well-oiled machine (like
standard bleed stealth malkavian group 1-2, weenie presence vote,
weenie potence - just any monomaniac deck that doesnt have complicated
cards (like veil))
In terms of finding the actual people, that's tougher. In geneva, we
ran many event to introduce the game to people, we did this on
saturday mornings at the games workshop shop and conventions for
example. Otherwise, friends and friends of friends will make the best
learners as you know they are already a good fit socially.

I also think that Ascendance needs to be looked at.

This is a card that almost always guarantees one pool. Having like
60-70 in your deck makes it very hard to oust you. In almost all games
we have played, nobody ever plays Wash or Sudden Reversal on this card
so this is basically a guaranteed card to get played.

Hardly any other card in the game has that effect.

Just saying.

I think 4 and 6 are fine numbers of players. I can't imagine thinking
those games don't work. The early dynamics are just a little
different than with 5. Maybe you just shouldn't bring so many
preconceptions to the table.

I even think a 7 player game is fine, but it's true that I've seen
some people get impatient with more than half of the turns not
directly affecting them.

Messages.Author: Aaron Clark
Messages.Body:
In LA the magic numbers are 4 and 5. I believe a lot of groups are
like that.

If your group won't play 4, then your VTES will suffer.

I know many players will not play a 6-player game. I did it recently,
and it wasn't great. We played with a 2-hour time limit, and it
wasn't enough time.

I think game rosters and sign-up sheets are a good idea for VTES,
although I think a lot of groups are too casual to implement them. If
you have to have a certain number of people, then the first X people
to confirm their interest get in the game. If you have 6 people in
your group, rotate who sits out each week.
